setlist.title: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancing In The Streets** (3 reviews): The opening Dancing was an awesome surprise, though the music afterward was harder to get excited about; A ripping Dancin' in the Streets opened the show and set a high-energy tone [20][25][26]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Minglewood was very high powered, with a hot Jerry jam [28]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Security held the concrete walkways until about halfway through Hell in a Bucket, when the crowd broke through [29]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bobby sprinted across the whole width of the stage during the bombs in Bertha [21]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Billy stood on both feet, pounding his drum kit hard, during Playin' into Samson [21]
- **I Can't Get No Satisfaction** (1 other source): A 14-second tease of The Last Time follows Satisfaction [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ramble On Rose**: cut on the recording [30]
- **I Can't Get No Satisfaction**: back after 111 archived shows (623 days) [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-24.132577.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 152 min [1]. Said about its sound: Tape pauses occur between songs in the first set [1]
- **gd1984-06-24.sbd.miller.27449.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 154 min; rated 3.75/5 by 20 [3]
- **gd84-06-24.nak.connor.4628.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 148 min; rated 3.83/5 by 23 [4]. Said about its sound: Streams well, though the audience is a bit too prominent in the quiet passages; Audience recording lacks bass definition, though still decent [18][19]
- **gd1984-06-24.165037.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 152 min [7]. Said about its sound: The Other One space is included within The Other One track [7]
- **gd1984-06-24.beyerm88.holbrook.burke.81627.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 154 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [10]

## Around the show

- Heavy rain turned the ground to deepening mud; the reviewer feared drowning and felt Jerry was sinking along with the crowd [20]
- Crowd estimated around 35,000 to 38,000, setting a SPAC attendance record despite monsoon-like rain [24]
- After this show SPAC restricted ticket sales for future shows [24]
- Dancing bodies were silhouetted against the night on the concrete walkways into the amphitheatre; rain and mud made finding friends confusing [24]
- Fans camped out at Saratoga beforehand, and it was pouring when the show started; mud splashed all night [25]
- A dancing tent stood along the road at the top of the hill [26]
- Fans slid on mudslides after the show; energy rippled through the audience in waves, captured on tape [28]
- Rain fell all afternoon; the reviewer played guitar for dancers under a covered walkway outside the venue [29]
- Reviewer finds the second set stronger than the first, and Jerry far more alert than a decade later [19]
- Reviewer has attended many rainy shows, including the Giants Stadium tornado show, but only here worried about drowning [20]
- Reviewer says few shows in the 80s or any era match this one; second-set versions were the most thrilling seen [21]
- Not the tightest or most melodic show, but very high in energy [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-24.132577.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac2496**: taped by Steve Hill; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Steve Hill, Transfer By Keo; Nakamichi CM100/CP4 Shotguns > Sony D5, Tapes:Maxell UDXLII 90's; Tapes Labelled:Nakamichi 100 Guns -… [1]
- **gd1984-06-24.sbd.miller.27449.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat [3]. Also: Nakamichi 300/CP1 recording, copied to cassette master, then to DAT [3]
- **gd84-06-24.nak.connor.4628.sbeok.shnf**: source: Aud> Nak300> CM> CDR> EAC(Secure Mode)> CDWave(Retracking Only)> Shnv3(MKW ACT) [4]
- **gd1984-06-24.165037.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII-S) [7]. Also: Tim Friend's Nakamichi 300 source supplies a 3:18 patch in the Drums to Space transition [7]
- **gd1984-06-24.beyerm88.holbrook.burke.81627.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Tim Burke; source: Beyer M88 > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX90 (No Dolby) [10]. Also: Tape flips fall after Ramble On Rose, after Deal, during Drums, and after Satisfaction [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by D.King Gallery: [Grateful Dead 6/24/1984 Saratoga Springs NY Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/Dead_Pass_840624.html) [31]
- Poster by Steven Rood Grateful Dead: [1984-06-24 Saratoga Performing Arts Center, Saratoga Springs, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-06-24-saratoga-performing-arts-center-saratoga-springs-ny-usa/) [32]
